title: Benchmark Q-values: $\mathcal{Q}_q$ predictions vs NNDC data ($2 \times 2 = 6 \times 6$, MAE $\approx 4.4\%$, zero fitting)
html:
Example. Benchmark Q-values: \mathcal{Q}_q predictions vs NNDC data (2 \times 2 = 6 \times 6, MAE \approx 4.4\%, zero fitting)

All predictions use \approx (derived from q). Experimental values from NNDC/ENSDF with stated uncertainties. Crossing convention: (1, -h_{\mathrm{A}}) throughout (unimodular, \det T = -1).

Table 1 --- q-weighted Q-values: 2 \times 2 block with 6 \times 6 shell factors, zero fitting.

The six benchmarks span the mass range, from light nuclei that need no shell corrections to heavy nuclei that do, so a single q-derived formula is tested across regimes. This is the primary method. Each generator log-ratio is classified as unbinding (u), rebinding (r), or spectator (uc), then q-weighted:

Q = |q \cdot \Sigma_u + q^{-1} \cdot \Sigma_r + \Sigma_{uc}| \times \kappa_q \times F_{\mathrm{shell}}(q) \times F_{I_{10}}(Z,N;q)

Here the q-weighted generator sum |q \cdot \Sigma_u + q^{-1} \cdot \Sigma_r + \Sigma_{uc}| is multiplied by the q-dependent factors \kappa_q, F_{\mathrm{shell}}(q), and F_{I_{10}}(Z,N;q), of which F_{\mathrm{shell}}(q) is the shell-correction factor detailed below.

See Table.

MAE \approx 4.4\%, RMS \approx 5.4\%, max |\delta| \approx 10.3\%.

All six benchmarks are within 11\%. Light nuclei ({}^3\mathrm{H}, {}^{14}\mathrm{C}) are within 2.2\% and need no shell corrections; heavy nuclei ({}^{60}\mathrm{Co}, {}^{90}\mathrm{Sr}, {}^{137}\mathrm{Cs}, {}^{210}\mathrm{Bi}) require the shell factors F_{\mathrm{deg2}} and F_{\mathrm{Pauli}} from the 6 \times 6 regular representation of H_3(q).

Shell correction factors (derived from q):

  • F_{\mathrm{deg2}} = 0.5904: Rosso--Jones weighted degree-2 torus knot suppression for shells \geq 5 (N > 28), computed as the quantum-dimension weighted average (J_{2,9} \cdot \mathrm{tr}(T_{2,9} \cdot \Delta) + J_{3,4} \cdot \mathrm{tr}(T_{3,4} \cdot \Delta)) / ((J_{2,9}+J_{3,4}) \cdot \mathrm{tr}(\Delta)) from the H_3(q) Markov trace of the beta-decay operator. The two degree-2 knots correspond to the \mu_2 (T_{3,4}, s = 2^2) and \mu_3 (T_{2,9}, s = 3^2) branches of the Kummer tower, matching the CRT decomposition \mathbb{Z}/6\mathbb{Z} \cong \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z}.
  • F_{\mathrm{Pauli}} = 0.6382: alternating-irrep projection for magic-number shells (filled N), computed as |\mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{alt}}(\Delta)| / |\mathrm{tr}(\Delta)| where \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{alt}} evaluates with eigenvalue \lambda = -q^{-1}.
  • Both are eigenvalue ratios of \Delta_\beta = T_{\mathrm{mix}} - T_{nn} in the 6 \times 6 regular representation of H_3(q), which decomposes as 1(\mathrm{sym}) \oplus 2(\mathrm{std}) \oplus 1(\mathrm{alt}).

Error propagation note. The prediction uncertainty \delta Q from \delta q_0 \approx 1.4 \times 10^{-9} is negligible (\sim 10^{-9} \text{MeV}). The dominant theoretical uncertainty is structural (model approximations in F_{\mathrm{shell}}), not parametric. All \sigma-separations are therefore |Q - \mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{exp}}| / \delta\mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{exp}}.
